question: What defines an immunization defaulter in a primary health care setting?

options.A: A child who has completed all routine immunizations
options.B: A child who misses a scheduled vaccine dose
options.C: A newborn who has received no vaccines at birth
options.D: A caregiver who refuses to register at the clinic

explanation: Missing a scheduled dose delays protection and categorizes the child as a defaulter requiring retrieval. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: Why is tracking immunization defaulters crucial for community health?

options.A: It prevents caregivers from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It increases the monthly funding allocation for clinics
options.C: It maintains herd immunity against dangerous diseases
options.D: It reduces the total number of children born locally

explanation: Consistent immunization coverage protects the entire community by preventing disease outbreaks among vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: Which factor represents a health system-related cause of defaulting?

options.A: Caregiver forgetting the exact appointment date
options.C: Vaccine stockouts at the health facility
options.D: Long distance from home to the clinic

explanation: When clinics run out of vaccines, caregivers are turned away and often fail to return, leading to default. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h2)

question: A mother stops bringing her baby for immunizations because clinic staff shouted at her. This is an example of what barrier?
explanation: Negative interpersonal behavior from health staff actively discourages caregivers from completing immunization schedules. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of the Child Health Register at a clinic?

options.A: To report vaccine manufacturing defects to the ministry
options.B: To track scheduled visits and identify missing doses
options.C: To record the daily financial revenue of the facility
options.D: To document the birth weights of all community mothers

explanation: The register lists all registered children and allows nurses to spot who has missed an appointment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: Why is the home-based child health card important during community outreach?

options.A: It proves the child has completed school enrollment
options.B: It provides an immediate portable record of vaccination history
options.C: It guarantees free transportation back to the health center
options.D: It replaces the need to keep clinic registers updated

explanation: The physical card allows health workers to check immunization status instantly during home visits or outreach sessions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: A community health worker finds several infants missing their measles vaccine in a remote ward. What should be done first?

options.A: Close the primary health facility until compliance improves
options.B: Wait until the next national immunization campaign
options.C: Report the entire community to local law enforcement
options.D: Conduct targeted home visits to counsel the caregivers

explanation: Active home visits allow health workers to engage directly with caregivers and address the reasons for missing doses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h4)

question: What is the main role of village health volunteers in defaulter tracking?

options.A: Administering injectable vaccines during home visits
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of the primary health center
options.D: Bridging the gap between the community and the health facility

explanation: Volunteers live within the community, making it easier to identify defaulters and link them back to clinic services. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h4)

question: How should a nurse respond to a caregiver who stopped immunizations due to fear of fever?

options.A: Ignore the concern and administer the injection immediately
options.B: Scold the caregiver for neglecting the health of the baby
options.C: Acknowledge the fear and explain that fever shows the vaccine is working
options.D: Advise the caregiver never to return to the clinic

explanation: Empathic counseling and accurate information help alleviate fears without shaming the caregiver. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: Which communication approach helps uncover hidden reasons for vaccine refusal?

options.A: Warning the caregiver about legal penalties
options.C: Interrupting the caregiver to save time
options.D: Asking open-ended questions to encourage dialogue

explanation: Open-ended questions allow caregivers to express their worries and misconceptions freely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: What does a high drop-out rate between Pentavalent 1 and Pentavalent 3 indicate?

options.A: The clinic is receiving too many vaccine supplies
options.B: Many children are defaulting after starting the series
options.C: Caregivers are completing all scheduled doses early
options.D: Birth rates in the community are dropping rapidly

explanation: A wide gap between initial doses and completion indicates high defaulting and poor retention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h6)

question: Why is regular evaluation of a defaulter retrieval program necessary?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health registers
options.B: To measure success and identify areas needing improvement
options.C: To increase the cost of purchasing vaccine supplies
options.D: To reduce the number of staff working in the facility

explanation: Evaluation helps health teams see if their tracking methods work and where adjustments are needed. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h6)
